notes:
Lead profile: small CS automation startup building templated reply workflows. Inbound from blog + free tier signup. Early discovery — technical but cost-sensitive. Key pain: 429s during peak morning batch jobs (not steady-state traffic) leading to user-visible failures. Quoted fragments from call: "We get a huge burst when scheduled digests fire at 09:00 — dozens of conversations hit at once and our worker pool can't absorb the 429s gracefully". Requirements/asks (bulletized):
- Need per-API-key concurrency ceilings and adjustable burst allowances (soft quota vs hard quota).
- Want webhook/alert on sustained 429s and per-route throttling visibility.
- Prefer graceful 429 signaling (Retry-After) and guidance on client-side exponential backoff with jitter.
- Interested in short burst credits or temporary capacity spikes (minute-level bursts) rather than long-term higher commit.
- Needs cost estimate for expected 800 req/min 2x morning spike and for baseline 50 req/min.
- Logs + trace correlation: link request-id -> token usage -> latency (important for debugging).
- Minimal compliance: SSO for admin console and basic audit logs.
POC plan: run hosted API simulation with traffic pattern file (attached), verify 429 ratios, latency p50/p95 under burst, test Retry-After headers and client backoff doc. Success criteria: <=1% failed requests after client backoff in 30min spike test; visibility into per-key quota consumption; documented fallback behavior when capacity constrained.
Notes on commercial: SMB pricing sensitivity — prefers usage-based with optional burst add-on. AE to draft 3 pricing scenarios (pay-as-you-go, burst-pack, monthly cap).
Open questions for infra: Can Redwood provide minute-level burst allowances with predictable Retry-After? How are concurrency limits enforced across streaming vs non-streaming endpoints? SE to validate with runtime team.
Important links: Drive pricing deck, Security questionnaire. Fireflies recording exists (ff_2026-02-24_qr-demo-1).
